title: Scenario-driven win grid: SDR quickplay (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, scenario-driven win grid for SDRs and AE pre-call planning. Not a polished deck — a sketch that maps buying triggers to punchy opening lines, demo asks, proof points, and fallback plays. Use as a one-pager to prep 5–8 minute discovery calls where we need to quickly qualify latency/cost/regulation pain and position Redwood as the safe, predictable inference partner.

How to use:
- Pick the scenario that most closely matches the prospect (or combine elements).
- Memorize 2–3 hooks and one measurable proof point.
- Start with the trigger question, then the pain validation, then the hack (how Redwood helps).
- End with a micro-commit: a short demo or a workload snapshot request.

Scenarios (high level) — quick pick:
1) Regulated Fintech — compliance + PII isolation required
   - Trigger events: SOC2/ISO audit, customer data residency request, upcoming funding round + security review
   - Opening hook: "Are you planning for an external compliance audit or moving customer data behind your VPC in the next 90 days? We help teams keep inference inside the customer network while giving devs a cloud-like API."
   - Key pain check: "How are you currently handling model hosting and audit logs for user data? Any blockers for keeping logs but not exposing raw PII?"
   - Redwood value props to surface: private deployment (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM integration, audit logs + token-level observability, SLA for dedicated capacity
   - Proof point: "Customer X (payments) reduced their external audit gaps by centralizing inference into a private deployment and cut token-cost variance by 23% after switching from ad-hoc GPUs."
   - Demo ask / next step: request network diagram + sample request volumes (top 3 endpoints) — propose a short technical kickoff to validate VPC peering and KMS flow.
   - Objection play: "We can't give access to data" → Suggest air-gapped evaluation using synthetic inputs and a local private deployment checklist; highlight that Redwood supports on-prem package.

2) High-throughput consumer SaaS — cost and latency optimization
   - Trigger events: growth spike, monthly inference bill > $Xk, user-facing latency complaints
   - Opening hook: "If you could cut per-session inference cost by 30% and shave 50–200ms off median response time without changing model UX, would you be interested in a quick cost/latency scan?"
   - Key pain check: "What's your current token spend and p50/p95 response time? Any burstiness in traffic?"
   - Redwood value props to surface: batching + KV-prefix caching, model quantization recommendations, dedicated pools for predictable throughput, routing policies for low-cost fallbacks
   - Proof point: "Trial with Customer Y (consumer search) moved heavy routes to dedicated pools and reduced 95th percentile latency from 1.2s to 420ms while lowering cost per thousand tokens by 28%."
   - Demo ask / next step: ask for one week of sample telemetry (or a Grafana export). Offer a short Optimize audit to surface quick wins.
   - Objection play: "We already tuned our model, can't save more" → Offer a baseline audit; point to batching and routing opportunities that don't require model changes.

3) Platform team / internal ML infra — standardization and developer experience
   - Trigger events: multiple teams building in-house model endpoints, repeated infra toil, rising incident MTTR for model endpoints
   - Opening hook: "Are your teams re-building model infra every quarter? We provide a unified runtime so platform teams can expose the same API and observability across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
   - Key pain check: "How many different infra patterns exist today? What is the average time to onboard a new model?"
   - Redwood value props to surface: single API across deployment modes, rollouts/canary tooling, token-level cost visibility, per-model dashboards
   - Proof point: "Platform Z reduced onboarding time from 6 weeks to 10 days using our model-onboarding templates and automated tracing hooks."
   - Demo ask / next step: request architecture diagram + one onboarding ticket to run a compatibility check.
   - Objection play: "We can't adopt a vendor runtime" → Emphasize private deployment and vendor-neutral runtimes; show how rollbacks and canaries work.

Quick win snippets (soundbites for calls) — pick one or two and use sparingly:
- "We help keep your model latency predictable while lowering per-token cost — without changing your model weights."
- "Private deployment + token-level observability so security and product teams can both sleep at night."
- "Two-hour optimize audit: we'll point to batching, a routing policy and one quantization change that typically pays back in weeks."

Competitive signals to listen for and how to respond:
- Prospect says they are evaluating HostA or CloudB managed endpoints: "Great — are they offering private deployments or per-route latency SLOs? Redwood uniquely routes per policy and has first-class private plane options."
- Prospect says they're building everything in-house: "Totally valid. Is the key blocker time to scale or predictable costs? We integrate with your CI and can run a side-by-side to show unit economics."
- Prospect mentions open models only: ask about inference cost and throughput; highlight Redwood's kernel selection + quantization recommendations to lower costs.

Suggested micro-deck outline for follow-up (4–6 slides)
- Slide 1: One-liner + relevant scenario headline + 30s ROI claim (cost or latency)
- Slide 2: Short architecture sketch (hosted/dedicated/private options visually)
- Slide 3: Measurable wins / case studies (1–2 bullets)
- Slide 4: Quick plan: audit, pilot, rollout (milestones + success metrics)
- Slide 5: Ask + next steps (tech kickoff & data request)

Field ops TODO (for SDRs & SEs)
- Keep a scatter file with past prospect telemetry snippets (p50/p95, token spend, burst factor).
- For pilots: capture the minimal data set — three endpoints, 7 days of traffic, and one representative prompt set.
- Prepare a one-page private-deploy checklist for security reviewers (network, KMS, audit logs).

Open questions / follow-ups for product/enablement:
- Can we get a one-page template for the Optimize audit output (plug-inable to sales attachments)?
- Request: a short A/B script for fairness/regression checks that SEs can run during pilots.

Notes to self / rough ideas (working):
- Consider a compact two-column card for each scenario: left = trigger + discovery questions, right = three short bullets for proof points/demo ask/objection play. Good for Slack copy.
- Add a short one-click data request form (SRE-friendly) so SDRs can ask for telemetry without long emails.

End of sketch — use, iterate, and push important bits into a canonical battlecard deck when validated in the field.
